thread.title: Dow Jones Leads As Apple, Boeing, McDonald's Rise | Investor's Business Daily

author: PAUL WHITFIELD
title: Dow Jones Leads As Apple, Boeing, McDonald's Rise | Investor's Business Daily
text:
The stock market continued to reward positive earnings reports Wednesday, as three Dow Jones components charged ahead. Meanwhile, preliminary trade talks got underway with China, and the Federal Reserve prepared to release its policy statement at 2 p.m. ET.
X The Dow Jones Industrial Average popped 1.3%, while the Nasdaq added 1%. Large caps in the S&P 500 rose 0.8%, but small caps in the Russell 2000 gauge tacked on just 0.3%.
Volume rose on both major exchanges vs. the same time in the previous session.
In the 30-component Dow Jones index, Boeing ( BA ) gapped up almost 7% after reporting a 19.7% earnings beat . Apple ( AAPL ), which reported late Tuesday , gapped up about 5% on earnings that were roughly in line. McDonald's ( MCD ) advanced about 3% after topping by 4% the Street's consensus view on earnings.
Internationally, McDonald's same-store sales increased 4.4% vs. views for 4%. Same-store sales domestically grew 2.3%, below the consensus estimate for 2.4%.
Alibaba Gaps Up Chinese retail marketplace Alibaba ( BABA ) gapped up 5% in heavy volume. Alibaba topped views by 6%. The megacap stock is 22% below a high notched in June.
China's Shanghai composite eased 0.7%, falling for a third consecutive session.
Breakouts in late morning trade included Mercury Systems ( MRCY ), up 14% in heavy volume after strong earnings; real estate investment trust Realty Income ( O ), up 1% in slow turnover; and managed health care provider Anthem ( ANTM ), up 10% in fast trade also on an earnings report.
Among IBD's 197 industry groups, internet retail was having a good day. Cars.com ( CARS ), an online platform for buying new and used vehicles, gapped up 7% in heavy volume. The stock is working on its sixth weekly gain in a row and is now 15% below its July high.
On the downside, household appliances and housewares were among the biggest losers. Tupperware ( TUP ) careened 28% lower after earnings matched expectations, but revenue missed. The stock is 53% off its 52-week high.
Economic News Analysts expect the Federal Reserve to stand pat on interest rates when it releases its announcement this afternoon.
In the meantime, China and the U.S. began trade talks. Few market watchers expect a breakthrough. The deadline for U.S. tariff increases to kick in is March 2. Pressure to make a deal will probably be more likely near the deadline.
The first take on fourth-quarter GDP was originally scheduled for this morning. But the government shutdown pushed release deadlines back. A new release date has not been set yet.
